briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the climate briefing for November 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🌍 Deepening Conflicts at COP31 over Fossil Fuel Phase-out and Climate Finance
sections.content: At the COP31 climate summit currently underway in Antalya, Türkiye, UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued a stark warning that 'peace cannot be built on a burning planet,' while Greta Thunberg also urged nations to take action, declaring that the Earth is being murdered [89, 128]. However, from the early stages of the summit, friction has flared among stakeholders regarding the future of fossil fuels and the acceleration of their phase-out; while the European Parliament delegation called for a phase-out, the presence of over 100 fossil-fuel-linked companies and organizations at the venue has sparked controversy [100, 114, 129]. Furthermore, urgent appeals by climate-vulnerable nations for climate finance assistance have met lukewarm responses from major economies, leaving negotiations at an impasse [99].

sections.title: 🔴 Accelerating Climate Disasters and Escalating Damage in Vulnerable Nations
sections.content: Despite bearing minimal responsibility for the greenhouse gas emissions driving climate change, Nepal—suffering severe devastation from recent Himalayan flash floods and burdened by mounting debt—has appealed to developed nations for prompt financial support [1, 124, 125]. Meanwhile, in Southeast Asia, the combined effects of El Niño and climate change have been analyzed to have exacerbated unprecedentedly destructive wildfires across Indonesia [98, 101, 121]. In addition, the Super El Niño phenomenon has prompted warnings of increased maternal mortality risks for millions of pregnant women in crisis-hit regions worldwide, while rapid sea temperature spikes off the California coast have triggered mass die-offs of marine life, turning ecological crises into reality [130, 133].

sections.title: ⚠️ South Korea's Climate Action Ranks Near Bottom: Policy Challenges Ahead
sections.content: In an international climate response assessment, South Korea received a poor report card, ranking 61st out of 68 evaluated countries and remaining near the bottom [7]. Concerns have been raised that an overreliance on overseas emission reductions in its greenhouse gas reduction pathway could undermine the fundamental spirit of the Paris Agreement [8]. Warning lights have also turned on for the domestic renewable energy deployment target of 100GW, with energy expansion hampered at the local level by a lack of grid connections [65, 75]. In addition, amid ongoing criticism over the lack of legal grounds for financial and tax support under the Green Transformation (K-GX) policy, the enactment of a Special Act on Carbon-Neutral Industries has emerged as an urgent priority [55].

sections.title: 🌱 Entering the Global 'Age of Electricity' and Renewable Energy Innovation
sections.content: Fatih Birol, Executive Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), declared that the world has moved beyond a system dominated by fossil fuels such as coal and oil, firmly entering an 'Age of Electricity' [131]. The IEA projected that global solar PV capacity will surge by 2.4 times over the next six years through 2031, adding 3.6TW, while city-level electrification competition is drawing attention as a key solution [76, 132]. Technological innovation continues domestically as well, with the Jeju Energy Corporation embarking in earnest on developing hybrid water electrolysis technology to address renewable energy intermittency [61, 63]. Furthermore, the Incheon City Corporation is accelerating a public-led green energy transition by utilizing idle public land—including the Susan and Gongchon water purification plants—to build 5.7MW of solar power generation facilities [78, 84].

sections.title: 🌱 Grassroots Carbon Neutrality Grounded in Local Communities and Agriculture
sections.content: To safeguard agricultural water security amidst the climate crisis, the Korea Rural Community Corporation discussed agricultural water management strategies with 14 nations and initiated the establishment of a preemptive prevention system for agricultural infrastructure [4, 13]. At the community level, the city of Uijeongbu has moved to expand urban carbon sinks by establishing a 'Carbon Neutrality Demonstration Garden' planted with high-carbon-absorbing shrubs [40, 48]. In Seoul, Nowon-gu was designated an Environmental Education City and is focusing on strengthening community-driven carbon neutrality capacity, while Gwanak-gu is running action campaigns promoting the use of reusables and tumblers [34, 37, 57]. The convergence of everyday action and the transformation of public infrastructure is yielding tangible progress in regional carbon neutrality [42, 58].

briefing.closing: Amid the tangible impacts of the climate crisis and the massive wave of the energy transition, more responsible policy implementation and practical solidarity are required. This concludes today's climate briefing.
